title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together
abstract: arXiv:2611.27911v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Transformer performance scales with depth, but layer count merely counts the opportunities for sequential computation: layers could still behave as nearly independent refinements that barely depend on one another. We study how transformers develop functional depth during pretraining, introducing an exact inclusion-exclusion decomposition that isolates the connected component, i.e., the computation that appears only when a specified set of layers acts together under identity ablation. Tracking this quantity across public checkpoints of Pythia, OLMo, and Amber yields three findings. First, write-relative connected coordination strengthens from its initialization or earliest-checkpoint baseline as pretraining proceeds, across all measured interaction orders. Second, these connected components are behaviorally consequential under direct intervention: deleting them damages perplexity more than deleting a norm-matched random direction at the s

translated_title: 功能深度是习得的：分离各层唯有协同作用才能产生的计算
translated_abstract: Transformer 的性能随深度提升而扩展，但层数只是统计了顺序计算的机会：各层仍可能表现为几乎相互独立的精细化处理，彼此之间几乎没有依赖。我们研究了 Transformer 在预训练过程中如何发展出功能深度，引入了一种精确的容斥分解方法，以分离出“连通分量”，即在恒等消融下，只有当一组指定层共同作用时才会出现的计算。通过在 Pythia、OLMo 和 Amber 的公开检查点上追踪这一量，我们得到三项发现。第一，随着预训练的进行，在所有测量的交互阶数上，“相对于写入的连通协调”都从其初始化或最早检查点的基线开始增强。第二，这些连通分量在直接干预下对模型行为具有实质性影响：删除它们对困惑度造成的损害大于删除一个范数匹配的随机方向……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出一种精确的容斥分解方法来分离“连通分量”（即各层唯有共同作用时才会产生的计算），并通过对 Pythia、OLMo、Amber 公开检查点的追踪发现这种跨层协同计算随预训练不断增强且删除它会显著损害模型性能，从而证明 Transformer 的功能深度是在训练过程中习得的。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces an exact inclusion-exclusion decomposition to isolate "connected components"—computations that emerge only when specified sets of layers act jointly—and shows by tracking Pythia, OLMo, and Amber checkpoints that such cross-layer coordination strengthens throughout pretraining and is critical to model behavior, demonstrating that functional depth is learned.
